gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the makers' cycle-life figures are measured to different end points: BLUETTI gives the Apex 300 'up to 6,000 cycles with 80% capacity retention', Anker gives the F3000 '4000 Cycles' with no end capacity anywhere on its US page, and ALLPOWERS' R3500 kit page says 'over 3,500 charging cycles' with no end capacity; none of them states that the F3000's 3,600 W is a total, with each household NEMA 5-20R outlet limited to 2,400 W and 3,600 W available only from the TT-30R RV outlet.
standout_why: I read StormWatts (cited, 2026-11-08), Lights On Labs (cited, 2026-10-27) and EnergySage (cited). StormWatts lists price, Wh, solar cap and panels for 24 kits but gives no AC continuous or surge figure and no cycle life. Lights On Labs gives one unlabelled 'output' figure per kit and no cycle life. EnergySage gives surge only for EcoFlow, Jackery and Goal Zero (continuous only for the BLUETTI Apex 300 and Anker), and has only a general line that LFP is 'typically rated for 3,000 charge cycles or more' without an end point. None of them gives a per-outlet limit. SolarGenAdvisor (cited) would not load because of a TLS certificate error, so I could not check it.
decides: It supports a split pick rather than reversing it. On paper the BLUETTI Apex 300 has the strongest durability claim, and it is the only one stated to a defined end point (6,000 cycles to 80%). But every Apex 300 kit is a pre-order that ships in late January 2027, so it is the option for a shopper who can wait. Of our kits, the ALLPOWERS R3500 + SP037 400 W ships now, has 3,200 W rated and 7,000 W peak, which clears the 3,000 W line, and costs $1,586.73 at the link price ($1,803.10 store), or about $0.50 per Wh. That makes it the ships-now value pick. Its 'over 3,500 cycles' has no end point, so it should not be ranked against BLUETTI's 6,000-to-80% claim. The cycle-count difference between the Anker F3000 ('4000 Cycles') and BLUETTI or ALLPOWERS is not a like-for-like comparison and should not decide the pick. The F3000's 3,600 W headline applies only through its TT-30R outlet.

findings.label: Cycle life and its stated end point
findings.value: up to 6,000 cycles to 80% capacity retention
findings.note: Maker's wording: 'With the EnerBalance AI system, enjoy up to 6,000 cycles with 80% capacity retention.' This is the only kit in the 3,000 W class whose cycle claim has a stated end capacity on the maker's US page.

findings.label: AC rating as stated
findings.note: The page gives no figure labelled surge or peak. 'Lifting Power' is BLUETTI's own term and is not defined on the page as surge, so it should not go in a surge column next to the other makers' figures without a footnote.

findings.label: Shipping state and price
findings.value: $2,199.00 store (list $2,399.00); 'expected to ship in late January'; 'Each unit will be delivered separately'
findings.note: Link price $2,089.05 (Kits we link table). $2,089.05 / 2,764.8 Wh = $0.756 per Wh. Refill at rated panel output: 2,764.8 Wh / 400 W = 6.9 h of full sun (arithmetic at rated output; real output is lower).

findings.label: Cycle life and its stated end point
findings.note: Spec table: Cycle Life '4000 Cycles'. The only '80%' on the page is a usage assumption in a savings example ('80% daily cycling'), not a retention spec. The page also says '10-Year Lifespan with InfiniPower', which is not a warranty.

findings.label: AC output per outlet vs headline
findings.value: NEMA 5-20R: 2,400 W max per outlet (total 3,600 W); TT-30R: 3,600 W max; AC surge 7,200 W; SurgePad 4,860 W
findings.note: The 3,600 W headline is the total across outlets. A single appliance on a standard household 20 A outlet gets at most 2,400 W (120 V × 20 A). The full 3,600 W on one plug needs the TT-30R RV outlet.

findings.label: Solar input limits
findings.note: The 2,400 W figure is the sum of two ports, and the low-voltage port takes only 800 W. The page listed the station alone at $2,599.00. The bundle price showed 'Price Loading' and did not resolve.

findings.label: Cycle life and AC rating as stated on the kit listing
findings.value: 'over 3,500 charging cycles' (no end capacity); 3,200 W pure sine wave (7,000 W peak)
findings.source_title: ALLPOWERS Solar Generator Kit 3200W (R3500 + SP037 400W Solar Panel)
findings.note: Read from the store's product data with storecheck.py. Store price $1,803.10 (compare-at $2,699), available true. Link price $1,586.73 (Kits we link): $1,586.73 / 3,168 Wh = $0.501 per Wh. Refill at rated output: 3,168 Wh / 400 W = 7.9 h of full sun (arithmetic at rated output). The listing also gives a 2,000 W max solar charge.

findings.product: ALLPOWERS SP037 400 W panel (in R3500 / S2000 Pro kits)
findings.label: Maker's own derating of the bundled panel
findings.source_title: ALLPOWERS Solar Generator Kit 2400W (S2000 Pro + SP037 400W Solar Panel)
findings.note: Wording on ALLPOWERS' own SP037 kit listing: 'This bundle solar panel is made of Polycrystalline silicon solar cells ... a 100W solar panel can output about 55W-65W.' Applied to 400 W, that is about 220–260 W, so about 12–14 h to refill the R3500's 3,168 Wh (arithmetic on the maker's own figure). The same store also has a listing titled 'SP037 Polycrystalline'. It is not confirmed that this text also appears on the R3500 kit page.

findings.label: AC rating as stated, and cycle life
findings.value: 3,600 W output, 7,200 W surge; X-Boost to 4,600 W (resistive loads); no cycle count stated, only '10 years of reliable power'
findings.note: Read from the store's product data with storecheck.py: $1,369.00, available true. The listing text does not say which panels, if any, are in this 'Solar Generator' listing, so I did not use it as a kit price. X-Boost is not continuous capacity for motor loads and should not be compared with other makers' rated watts.

findings.label: What the cited rivals state on these points
findings.value: None of StormWatts, Lights On Labs or EnergySage gives a cycle-life end point; StormWatts and Lights On Labs give no surge figure; none gives a per-outlet limit
findings.source_title: Solar Generator Kits Compared at the Same Panel Watts (StormWatts)
findings.note: Also read https://www.lightsonlabs.com/power-stations/best-solar-generators/ and https://www.energysage.com/energy-storage/solar-generators-overview/ on 2026-11-17. EnergySage's Apex 300 row ($2,099 with two 200 W panels) does not match today's BLUETTI store price ($2,199).

unsourced: Jackery HomePower 3000: cycle life with its end point, continuous and surge watts, per-outlet limits, and the current kit price and dispatch state. jackery.com returned HTTP 429 on four attempts (two product URLs plus the store tool). A search snippet said '4,000 cycles to 70%' and '7,200 W surge', but I did not open a page that states it, so it is left out. StormWatts said 'ships from Nov 28' on 2026-11-08, which I did not check against Jackery's store.

ALLPOWERS R3500: the end capacity behind 'over 3,500 cycles'. A search snippet said the manual states about 3,500 cycles to 80% and about 6,500 to 50%, but the manuals.plus copy returned 403 and iallpowers.com returned 429 for the station page. Per-outlet AC limits were not on the kit listing.
EcoFlow DELTA 3 Ultra: cycle count and end point, and a priced bundle with 2× 220 W panels. The us.ecoflow.com product page returned 429, and the store data shows no cycle figure.
BLUETTI Apex 300 and Apex 200: per-outlet AC limits, a figure BLUETTI labels as surge or peak, and the Apex 200 cycle end point. I did not open an Apex 200 page within the tool budget.

Anker SOLIX F3000 + 400 W bundle price on ankersolix.com: the price area showed 'Price Loading'. StormWatts reported $2,299.99 with code ($2,599.99 store) on 2026-11-08; I did not confirm it at the maker today.
SolarGenAdvisor's '3000 watt' page (cited by ChatGPT): would not load because of a TLS certificate error, so I could not check whether it states cycle end points or per-outlet limits.
